paragraphs: It's eight o'clock, and May is in Grandma's kitchen. She has a lot of homework, and her pencil is very short. "I'm very tired," she says. "I need a break." She eats a banana and looks at her book again. Grandma is in the living room. Pat is in bed in the room upstairs. The house is very quiet.

Then Pat comes into the kitchen with his blanket. His face is white. "May, I'm afraid," he says. "I had a bad dream about spiders." "They're in the basement, and they're big!" "There aren't any spiders, Pat," says May. "Listen! There's a noise downstairs," says Pat. May stops. She listens. "Yes," she says. "I can't say what it is."

"Don't wake Grandma," says May. "We're going to look." Pat holds her hand, and they go down. "Where is the noise?" asks May. "I'm not afraid," says May. But her hand is cold. In the basement, a small lamp is on. The noise comes from a big white machine. "It's Grandma's washing machine!" says May. Pat laughs and laughs. "We're brave!" he says. May takes him back to bed, and he sleeps.
